programme: TCF7, NR4A3, RUNX1 and IKZF2 converge on a shared T-cell-receptor/IL-2 circuit that sets T-cell differentiation state: TCF7 (with LEF1) marks stem-like/progenitor T cells and drives their effector genes (IFNG, IL2, IL17A, CD4); NR4A3 is the immediate-early TF induced by chronic TCR/CD28 signalling (targets ITK, BTK, CD28, IL2, IL4) that pushes cells toward exhaustion and also acts in myeloid cells (mast cell/macrophage reprogramming); RUNX1 sits upstream of CD4/CD8/GATA3 lineage commitment and integrin-mediated leukocyte adhesion (ITGAL, ITGAX, CSF2); IKZF2/Helios locks in Treg identity via FOXP3 and IL2RA. Together they describe the transcriptional switch from effector to exhausted/regulatory T-cell states under chronic antigen or inflammatory exposure.
role_in_a: In COPD, this circuit is expected to mark the shift of airway-infiltrating T cells from effector to exhausted/regulatory phenotypes under chronic smoke- or infection-driven antigen exposure: TCF7 and RUNX1 both surface in an immune-dysregulation/shared-airway-disease signature, and RUNX1 is separately described as dual-acting in inflammation-driven chronic disease, while NR4A3 modulates inflammatory/vascular remodeling elements in the diseased airway.
role_in_b: In ovarian cancer, the same circuit governs the state of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes and adjacent myeloid cells: TCF7+ cells mark an expanding tumor-reactive, stem-like T-cell subpopulation in ovarian TIL, NR4A3-high mast cells reprogram tumor-associated macrophages and NR4A3 also modulates PARP-inhibitor (niraparib) sensitivity, RUNX1 is strongly upregulated in the tumor immune compartment (Open Targets 0.94th percentile), and IKZF2 marks Treg identity within the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment.
shared_axis: Both tissues subject T cells to sustained antigenic/inflammatory stimulation — cigarette-smoke/pathogen-driven chronic airway inflammation in COPD, tumor-antigen-driven chronic stimulation in ovarian TIL — and both appear to resolve that stimulation through the same TCF7-progenitor / NR4A3-exhaustion / RUNX1-lineage / IKZF2-Treg switch, so the two diseases converge on a shared immune-exhaustion axis rather than a shared tissue programme.
reasoning: TCF7 and NR4A3 are each independently and specifically placed in both diseases by the retrieved papers, and T-cell exhaustion/Treg biology is separately well established as central to both chronic COPD airway inflammation and the ovarian tumor immune microenvironment, so the connection follows from each disease's own immunology rather than from a stated joint fact. It stops short of strong because RUNX1 has no ovarian-specific mechanistic paper (only a high Open Targets score) and IKZF2 has no COPD evidence at all, so two of the four carrying factors are placed in only one disease; note also that these four sit in the mid-range of the count distribution (69-73/208), below BRCA1 (79) and HOXC6 (75), which were not used because their individual evidence did not cohere into a joint mechanism.
support: 42196213 (COPD: TCF7 within a three-gene immune-dysregulation airway signature); 40637995 (ovarian cancer: TCF7-expressing tumor-reactive T cells expand in TIL); 40679522 (ovarian cancer: Wnt/β-catenin pathway markers, TCF7's partner pathway, in ascites tumor cells); 39985498 (ovarian cancer: lncRNA-driven cisplatin resistance via an IL-12-linked axis touching TCF7 target space); 38474099 (COPD: NR4A2/NR4A3 modulate inflammatory pathway elements); 34768801 (COPD-relevant: NR4A3 in vascular/cardiovascular remodeling); 41026279 (ovarian cancer: NR4A3 upregulation increases niraparib sensitivity); 40789260 (ovarian cancer: NR4A3-high mast cells reprogram tumor-associated macrophages, promoting metastasis); 42653451 (COPD: RUNX1 in shared epithelial/immune airway-disease architecture); 41463011 (inflammation-driven disease: dual role of RUNX1); 30485824 (ovarian cancer: incidental IKZF2 rearrangement in a cell-line genomic survey, weak).
how_to_falsify: Take paired single-cell RNA-seq/ATAC-seq of CD8+ and Treg T cells from COPD airway biopsies and ovarian tumor TIL from the same or comparable patients, and test whether TCF7-high progenitor-like and NR4A3/IKZF2-high exhausted/Treg populations share the same chromatin accessibility and TF motif enrichment (TCF7/LEF1, NR4A, RUNX, IKZF motifs) across the two tissues. If the exhaustion/Treg states in COPD T cells use a distinct, non-overlapping regulatory grammar from ovarian TIL — or if NR4A3 perturbation reverses exhaustion markers in one tissue's T cells but not the other's — the shared-axis claim is falsified.
caveats: Only 4 independent cohort pairs underlie the 208 patient-group comparisons, so the 69-79/208 recurrence reflects repeated stratification (stage, sex, smoking status, etc.) within a small number of source studies, not broad independent replication. Only a single-view exclusion list was supplied for this pair (no explicit tissue-generic list); the excluded single-view factors (PAX2, HOXA10, ESRRB, ID1, PROX1) are reproductive/Müllerian developmental TFs specific to one ovarian subgroup, which supports leaving the hormone/Müllerian axis out of the account rather than reaching for it. RUNX1's ovarian placement rests on an Open Targets score with no disease-specific mechanistic paper in the given material, and IKZF2 has no COPD evidence at all — both are weaker links than TCF7 and NR4A3, so treat the module as an immune-exhaustion hypothesis rather than a settled joint mechanism. BRCA1, ESR1, XBP1 and MECOM had good disease-specific evidence individually but were excluded because they define separate axes (DNA repair/estrogen signalling, ER-stress/UPR, hematopoietic-vascular regulation) that do not cohere with the T-cell circuit or with each other into one shared story.
